title: TS SDK: Convertible stream proxy with backpressure-aware retry recipes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal:
Implement a lightweight, well-documented "convertible stream proxy" in the TypeScript SDK that lets callers seamlessly convert between AsyncIterable and WHATWG ReadableStream (Web Streams) while preserving backpressure semantics and enabling deterministic retry behavior on transient network/inference errors.

Background / motivation:
- Users keep asking for easy patterns to consume the same streaming LLM responses in web apps (ReadableStream) and Node/deno services (AsyncIterable) without duplicating adapter code.
- Current adapters either drop backpressure semantics, swallow cancellations, or make retry behavior undefined (leading to doubled-up outputs or truncated responses after a transient error).
- We need a pragmatic, ergonomic primitive that:
  1) Converts AsyncIterable<T> -> ReadableStream<T> and ReadableStream<T> -> AsyncIterable<T> with consistent cancellation semantics.
  2) Exposes configurable high-water/low-water thresholds and a bounded in-memory buffer; default profile favors low-latency (small buffer) for interactive chat.
  3) Supports checkpointed retry semantics for idempotent streaming operations (e.g., resume from last complete token boundary when feasible).

Acceptance criteria:
- Library export: "convertibleStreamProxy" (well-typed generic) + small helpers: "asyncIterableToWebStream", "webStreamToAsyncIterable", "CheckpointedRetryPolicy".
- Default behavior: preserves backpressure and propagates cancellation/abort reason across the conversion boundary.
- Retry semantics: transparent retry for transient transport errors when upstream indicates resumability; otherwise surface a clear error.
- API examples: at least three cookbook recipes in the SDK docs: "browser chat consumer", "server-side fanout to multiple async consumers", "resumable embedding ingestion with checkpointing".
- Unit + integration tests covering: cancellation propagation, buffer watermark behavior, retry resume on provided checkpoint token, and memory usage under synthetic high-throughput.
- Performance target: conversion overhead <5% p90 compared to raw consumers (measured in toy benchmark harness).
- Internal docs: design doc + decision log in Confluence; example PR linking to benchmark results and e2e tests.

Design notes / proposal summary:
- Primitive core: a lightweight proxy with a bounded ring buffer and an internal state machine for {open, draining, aborted, closed}.
- Backpressure model: Web Streams push uses enqueue() but will respect strategy sizes; AsyncIterable consumer awaits when buffer empty. Use explicit Promise-based awaiters to bridge both models without relying on platform heuristics.
- Cancellation: pass an AbortSignal through the proxy. If upstream is aborted, push a terminal marker to downstream and include the original abort reason. If downstream aborts, propagate immediately to upstream and stop enqueuing.
- Checkpointing: caller-visible "checkpoint token" is an opaque string produced at stable boundaries (e.g., sentence or token delimiting event). The server-side retry protocol must support a resume token; our example will assume the model server can accept a resume cursor. When a transient error occurs and a resume token exists, the proxy will call the supplied retry hook to re-establish the stream from the cursor and continue enqueuing missing items.
- Retry policy: configurable policy object with: maxAttempts, backoffBaseMs, backoffFactor, shouldRetry(error, lastCheckpoint). Provide a default conservative policy (3 attempts, exponential backoff starting 250ms) used by example recipes.

API sketch (non-normative):
- function convertibleStreamProxy<T>(opts?: { highWater?: number; lowWater?: number; abortSignal?: AbortSignal; retryPolicy?: CheckpointedRetryPolicy<T> }) => { toWebStream(): ReadableStream<T>; toAsyncIterable(): AsyncIterable<T>; push(item: T, checkpoint?: string): void; close(): void; error(err: Error): void }
- Expose helpers that wrap typical SDK streaming responses so customers can call: 
  const proxy = convertibleStreamProxy();
  const rs = proxy.toWebStream(); // pass to fetch response body or Response.stream
  // server-side: for await (const chunk of proxy.toAsyncIterable()) { ... }

Implementation notes / trade-offs:
- We intentionally keep the primitive minimal and implement higher-level semantics (eg. token-boundary checkpointing heuristics) as examples in the cookbook rather than as core library complexity.
- We avoid dependence on experimental Node stream internals so this works in Node, Deno, and browsers.
- Memory considerations: bounded buffer default to 32 items or 64KB, whichever hits first; expose tuning options.

Docs & Examples to ship with the PR:
- docs/sdk/streams/convertible-proxy.md (cookbook with code samples for browser + server + resume scenarios)
- examples/ts/resumable-embeddings.ts (ingest large dataset with checkpointing)
- examples/ts/browser-chat-stream.html (demo page that consumes Web Stream directly)

Benchmarks / validation plan:
- Microbenchmark harness in tests/bench/stream-proxy-bench.ts that measures p50/p90 overhead for a synthetic 1MB stream split into 512-byte chunks.
- Load test in a staging cluster with representative model and 200 concurrent interactive sessions; measure memory consumption and p95 latency vs current adapter.

Security & compliance:
- No secrets stored in the proxy. Resume tokens are opaque and treated as PII only if they encode user data — examples will show token values as server-issued opaque IDs.

Rollout plan:
- Feature branch + unit tests -> internal canary docs + example playground -> ship behind feature flag in SDK 2026.04 (default enabled) -> monitor SDK consumer regressions for 2 weeks.

2026-03-11 - Marcus Chen: Implemented a prototype proxy to validate backpressure signals between a Node async iterator and a browser ReadableStream; prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3284 (WIP).
2026-03-11 - Design review: Decided to keep token-boundary heuristics out of core; examples will include a 'sentence-boundary' helper for chat use cases.
2026-03-12 - QA note: Integration test failing intermittently under high-throughput due to race on close() while retry in-flight; Marcus investigating and added a determinism test case.

2026-03-12 - Product feedback (Lena Ortiz): Ensure docs include migration guidance from existing adapters and include an example that demonstrates graceful fallback to a smaller model when retrying fails.
Follow-ups: add a small observability hook that emits lightweight telemetry for restart/resume counts (opt-in via config) and include guidance in release notes.
Blocked/risks: depends on server-side resume token semantics for best UX; if backend cannot provide stable resume cursor we will fallback to surface errors and document behavior.
